title: Meteorologist and GIS Developer
description:
Overview
Lynker is seeking a sharp Meteorologist and GIS Developer to support a long term contract with the Weather Prediction Center (WPC) and will have direct interaction with scientists within NOAA as well as partners outside of NOAA. This includes; NCEP centers, NWS weather forecast offices, NOAA research facilities, academia, and the NWS Science and Operations Officer community. In this capacity the incumbent will work with the above partners to develop new forecaster tools applied to operational and experimental forecasts. The work will also strive to build the capacity to enhance impact decision support services (IDSS), effectively building a Weather Ready Nation.
In addition, the incumbent will work to provide enhancements that build upon current forecaster tools as well as work to develop new services and forecaster tools. Promising work will be transitioned to operations. The incumbent will provide training materials on the enhanced forecaster products and tools.
Areas of particular need and interest to be addressed include developing forecaster tools for heavy precipitation associated with land-falling tropical cyclones, warm-season convection, winter storms, and atmospheric rivers. Additional areas of focus include the use of ensemble model output to aid forecaster generation of probabilistic products, as well as exploring future roles of weather forecasters.
The ideal Meteorologist and GIS Developer will currently be able to develop tools featuring mapped data. Assignments are typically received in terms of expected outcomes and incumbents are expected to act independently to develop required information, including selecting approach, and to provide sound analyses and recommendations. Assigned projects may include analysis, application development, or other areas specific to the assignment.
Responsibilities
Duties of the Meteorologist and GIS Developer will include the following:

• Collaborate with meteorologists at NCEP, NWS field offices, academia, and outside partners to develop forecast tools from short to medium range time frames.

• Use scientific and technical meteorological expertise to develop tools for determination of hazard information (rainfall, snowfall, temperatures).

• Develop web applications using modern industry languages and tools.

• Coordinate with NWS staff and external researchers to develop improved forecast tools.

• As appropriate, contribute to formal scientific publications, and/or attending off-site conferences, symposia and hazardous-weather-related outreach events.

• Perform related duties as assigned.

• Collaborate to transition forecaster tools and web services developed at WPC and elsewhere within NOAA into operations at WPC and other NOAA offices.

• Develop training materials to transition new tools and techniques into operations.

Qualifications
The Ideal Meteorologist and GIS Developer will have the following:

• Advanced degree in meteorology, hydrology or related earth science fields (MS or above preferred)

• Experience with deterministic and ensemble prediction system data sets and their application to hazardous weather diagnosis and prediction.

• Knowledge of weather forecasting - short to medium range

• Experience with GIS, GeoTiff, JSON, GeoJSON

• Knowledge of React, JavaScript, Zarr, Cloud Services, and Version Control Systems

• Experience with software development support in a team environment

• Experience with Python and shell scripting within a UNIX/Linux Environment.

• Ability to organize, plan, and complete projects

• Excellent written and oral communication skills for documentation and presentations

About Lynker
Lynker is a growing, employee owned business, specializing in professional, scientific and technical services. title: Research Intern, Inference (Summer 2027)

The Inference Research team is dedicated to building the next generation of efficient, scalable, and reliable serving systems for large foundation models, directly contributing to the mission of advancing open and transparent AI. Our work operates at the critical intersection of cutting-edge model architectures, high-performance systems engineering, and deep hardware optimization. We focus on co-designing software, algorithms, and models to significantly lower the cost and latency of modern AI systems.

As a research intern, you will dive into the complexities of distributed inference, compiler-aware optimization, and novel inference-time computation strategies (such as speculative decoding and phase-aware execution). • Familiarity with Transformer architectures and recent developments in foundation models

• Publications at leading conferences in machine learning or systems (i.e., MLSys, ICLR ).

The BESS Quality Engineer II (Warranty Management) is responsible for leading the end-to-end administration of warranty claims across utility-scale Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects. We're hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer to reinvent how Certa gets implemented. Because our no-code Studio lets you configure a workflow simply by describing it - Vibe Configuration℠ - one person can now sit with the customer, understand a requirement as it's spoken, and build it live, so they see their own workflow running in the same session. You'll work directly with Fortune 500 teams across compliance, information security, privacy, legal, procurement, finance, and sustainability - credible enough to discuss vendor-tiering policy with a Chief Procurement Officer, then open Studio and build it. You'll be one of the first people doing this, which means you'll also define how it's done.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Understand the business process: Run discovery and design sessions with Fortune 500 teams across compliance, security, privacy, legal, procurement, finance, and sustainability - often in the same room with competing views - and learn how their third-party processes actually run today, including the parts that live in email, spreadsheets, and people's heads.

- Document & optimize it: Map the current state and agree a target state against the metrics customers actually care about - onboarding cycle time, assessment turnaround, reviewer effort, audit readiness. You're not there to digitize a bad process faithfully, and a workflow that's technically correct but painful to use won't get adopted - so reviewer effort and drop-off are your problem, not theirs.

- Configure & automate it in Certa: Build the workflows, forms, logic, risk scoring, and approvals in Studio using Vibe Configuration℠ - live in the room wherever possible - plus the integrations and data flows into existing systems, and debug them when they break.

- Own the delivery: Own the plan, governance, and test cycle (scenarios and cases, SIT, UAT with the customer's own testers, sanity and regression), then cutover, go-live, hypercare, and a clean handover - accountable for the date and the success metrics behind it.

- Bring learning back from the front lines: Find the platform's real limits before anyone else does and bring them to Product with evidence - the customer, the frequency, the cost of the workaround - and turn what you built into templates and accelerators, so the next deployment starts ahead of where yours did.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

- Experience: 3+ years in customer-facing technical delivery - forward deployed engineering, solutions architecture, implementation consulting, or technical professional services.

- Hands-on technical skills: Comfortable with REST APIs, JSON, webhooks, and data mapping; able to script in Python or JavaScript and debug a failure across two systems you didn't build.

- Production LLM experience: You've worked with LLMs in production rather than in demos - prompts, retrieval, agent workflows, and evaluating output systematically rather than by vibes.

- Product-centric & shipping-biased: You think about the user in front of the screen, not the requirement in the document, and favor shipping something usable and iterating over shipping something perfect and late.

- Delivery fluency: You've carried a go-live date in front of a customer, so project plans, RAID logs, phase gates, test scenarios and cases, SIT, UAT, and regression testing are familiar ground.

- Communication: Thoughtful and streamlined - you listen first, hold your own with a Chief Procurement Officer, privacy counsel, and security architect in the same room, and can say no to a customer

La biométrie joue un rôle central dans les processus de recherche, d’identification et de vérification des identités. L’exploitation de caractéristiques physiques uniques, telles que les empreintes digitales ou les traits du visage, permet d’améliorer la fiabilité des recherches, de limiter les erreurs d’identification et de renforcer l’efficacité des processus opérationnels. L’évolution de ces technologies apporte également de meilleures capacités de comparaison, d’analyse et d’automatisation, tout en répondant à des exigences accrues en matière de sécurité et de qualité des données.
Le programme ABIS (Automated Biometric Identification System) vise à moderniser les capacités biométriques en remplaçant le système actuel de capture et de gestion des empreintes digitales. Cette nouvelle solution a pour objectif d’améliorer les performances et la qualité des traitements liés aux empreintes, tout en introduisant ou en renforçant les fonctionnalités de biométrie faciale. Grâce à des mécanismes de comparaison plus avancés et à une plateforme centralisée et évolutive, ce programme soutiendra une recherche biométrique plus précise, facilitera l’identification des personnes et répondra aux besoins futurs en gestion de l’identité.

As Preply grows into new markets and subject areas, the work gets more complex - and the impact gets bigger.

If you’re energized by data, problem solving, and leading cross-functional improvements, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

We’re looking for a Senior Expansion Experience Specialist to own the customer experience across Preply’s expansion - new geographies and subject areas. You’ll track and own key metrics for both learners and tutors and lead the cross-functional programs that move them.

You’ll also define the CX foundation for every expansion: the policies that govern learner and tutor interactions, the end-to-end user journeys, and the processes that make each launch work. You’ll work closely with Product, Growth, Customer Care, Supply Operations, and Localization, acting as the CX voice in decisions that affect learners and tutors at scale.

Key responsibilities:

- Own CSAT, contact rate, and other leading experience indicators for learners and tutors.

- Monitor performance, spot trends, and diagnose root causes.

- Turn data and customer insights into clear recommendations for Product, Growth, Customer Care, Supply Operations, and Localization.

- Lead cross-functional programs end-to-end - scoping, alignment, execution, and impact tracking.

- Build a feedback loop between expansion markets and global teams - turning local learnings into company-wide improvements.

2. Own Policy and Processes for New Markets & Subjects

- Map end-to-end user journeys for learners and tutors; identify friction points and drive structural fixes.

- Define and document the CX processes each new expansion requires, ensuring they’re scalable and built right from day one.

- Drive alignment on policies and processes across Product, Growth, Customer Care, Supply Operations, and Localization.

title: Research Fellow: AI-moderated Interviews at Scale: The Trust in Healthcare Study
description:
Surgo Health is requesting proposals for research projects building on our dataset focused on the healthcare trust landscape. While declining public trust in the U.S. healthcare system is widely documented through conventional survey methods, the underlying, individual-level drivers of this erosion often remain unclear.

To address this gap, our dataset explores trust dynamics across medical providers, health institutions, social media, and artificial intelligence, while highlighting actionable pathways for restoring confidence. The data encompasses both a detailed questionnaire battery and in-depth qualitative dialogues gathered by Derin®, our AI-moderated interviewing system.

Designed as a randomized, counterbalanced study, the dataset enables direct methodological comparisons between standard survey approaches and AI-moderated conversational interviews. It spans roughly 2,000 respondents across two distinct research panels. It has 6,000 completed interviews alongside extensive survey batteries, standard demographic indicators, and population weighting factors.

We are seeking research proposals that:

•
Advance the narrative on trust & healthcare -contribute to contemporary thinking on this subject in the U.S.

•
Leverage the conversations - projects should examine the reasoning, experiences, or context revealed when respondents elaborate, going beyond what closed items already capture.

•
Use the dataset - research questions should be answerable with the current dataset and not require funding for new data collection

•
Publishable - proposals should aim for peer-reviewed publication, with rigorous methodology.

We encourage proposals that move beyond showing that conversational interviews produce more detail, focusing instead on for whom, under what conditions, and through what mechanisms conversational data adds value. Projects will be given access to the full dataset and documentation, and can integrate external data (such as ACS, provider density, or state health policy indicators) via the harmonized geographic and demographic variables in the dataset.

Research Focus Areas

We welcome proposals in areas below, but also encourage you to submit proposals that are adjacent to these areas.

•
Trust in healthcare - drivers of trust erosion and recovery; public perspectives on AI in healthcare; decisions made against medical advice; institutional versus individual trust; and perceptions of the pharmaceutical industry.

•
Survey methodology - variations in response quality by education, age, income, geography, and political views; order and carry-over effects across modes; effort signatures; construct validity of trust items; and turn-level drop-off in conversational surveys.

•
Interviewer design and conversation dynamics - probing strategies and sequencing; respondent responses (elaboration vs. new disclosures); interviewer neutrality; and managing sensitive disclosures.

•
Computational methods - analysis pipelines for transcript data, including predicting closed-ended responses from conversational text (and vice versa).

Proposals should be 1-2 pages and outline:

•
Core contribution - how the research builds beyond existing literature

•
Use of qualitative data - what insights the conversational responses provide beyond standard closed-ended items.

•
Practical application - key decisions or practice changes informed by the findings.

•
Analytical plan - key variables, panel-specific estimates, and analytical approaches for randomized and observational factors.

•
Publication goals - target journals and expected outputs.

Program Structure

•
Surgo Health will select two to three proposals based on:

• Practical relevance and research depth

• Feasibility with available data

• Alignment with Surgo Health research priorities

• Potential for publication in high-impact journals

Selected projects will receive:

•
Stipend amount: $6,000 in compensation upon successful submission of draft to Surgo

• Weekly touch-point me

title: Product Manager
description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

We're looking for a Product Manager for Fraud & Risk who wants to understand how fraud really happens and to build products that stop it at scale. You're comfortable with ambiguity and you like hard trade-offs, like loss vs. friction or automation vs. human review. Your decisions rest on data, customer insight and strong cross-functional partnerships. And last, but not least, you know that a team succeeds because of its people, and you want to help build an environment where we can all do our best work.

This is a chance to shape the risk platform behind one of the largest restaurant payments businesses in the US. You'll use machine learning and AI to protect restaurants and help Toast grow. 

Who We Are

The Fraud & Risk team keeps Toast, our restaurants and their guests safe from fraud and financial loss. We also make it fast and easy for restaurants to get onboarded and get paid. The team owns:

• Merchant onboarding and underwriting (KYC/KYB)

• Transaction and payout risk monitoring

• The fraud rules and decisioning platform

• Settlement reserves

• Chargebacks and disputes

Our job is to balance loss prevention against growth. We stop bad actors without adding friction for the great majority of restaurants that are doing the right thing. We work closely with Risk Operations, Payments, Compliance and Legal. We operate like a small startup with high ambitions and a focus on speed, experimentation and iteration.

A day in the life (Responsibilities) 

• Drive and prioritize the roadmap for your area of Fraud & Risk. Balance fraud loss reduction, merchant experience and business growth.

• Set the strategy for detecting and preventing fraud across the merchant lifecycle: onboarding, payments, payouts and disputes.

• Partner with data science and engineering to improve risk models, rules and decisioning. Define the right trade-offs between catching fraud and avoiding false positives.

• Build AI-driven automation that scales our risk and chargeback operations, such as agent-assisted reviews and automated dispute responses.

• Understand the needs of restaurants, their guests and our internal Risk Operations analysts. Use customer conversations, investigations, data analysis, ops feedback and industry intelligence.

• Define and own success metrics such as fraud loss rates, chargeback rates and win rates, auto-approval rates and operational efficiency.

• Work with Compliance, Legal, Payments and external partners such as processors, card networks and risk vendors to deliver solutions that are compliant and scalable.

• Write clear product requirements and work closely with designers and engineers to bring them to life.

• Be a great teammate, always.

What you'll need to thrive (Requirements)

• 3+ years of product management experience, ideally in fraud, risk, payments, fintech, or trust & safety

• A working knowledge of the payments ecosystem: card networks, processors and acquirers, chargebacks and disputes, and KYC/KYB

• Strong analytical skills. You're comfortable digging into data yourself, with SQL as a strong plus, and you understand how ML models and rules engines make decisions.

• Sound judgment in weighing risk against customer friction, and the ability to make good calls with incomplete information, including during live fraud incidents

• Proven ownership of a product that supports company strategy and meets defined business objectives

• A track record of working well with cross-functional partners, especially operations, compliance and legal teams

• The ability to thrive and self-prioritize across multiple projects in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines

• Active use of AI tools and best practices in your own work to drive efficiency

• Exceptional attention to detail

OUR MISSION

At Redwood, we empower our customers with lights-out automation for their mission-critical business processes.

ABOUT US

Redwood Software is the leader in full stack automation fabric solutions for mission-critical business processes. With the first SaaS-based composable automation platform specifically built for ERP, we believe in the transformative power of automation. Our unparalleled solutions empower you to orchestrate, manage and monitor your workflows across any application, service or server - in the cloud or on premises - with confidence and control.

Redwood’s global team of automation experts and customer success engineers provide solutions and world-class support designed to give you the freedom and time to imagine and define your future. Get out of the weeds and see the forest, with Redwood Software.

CORE VALUES

One Team. One Redwood

Make Your Own Weather

Obsess over Customer Success

Work the Problem

Be Curious

Own the Outcome

Respect Each Other

YOUR IMPACT 

We are seeking a Senior Deal Desk Analyst to join our Revenue Operations team. This role will primarily support our sales teams outside the United States, with a focus on EMEA. The Senior Deal Desk Analyst is responsible for providing crucial administration and operational support to the sales team in order to facilitate quote and order execution while enhancing efficiency. They will actively work with sales, legal, finance, and other cross functional teams on deal structuring and commercial terms to ensure compliance and optimize operational processes to drive successful order execution. They will act as an internal contact across functional back office teams to ensure that customer proposals are structured and processed according to the requests of the customer but also the company's policy. They will provide proactive guidance throughout the lifecycle of sales opportunities from the initial solution identification through closure. 

• Drive deal review discussions with the Sales organization.

• Collaborate with the Legal, Finance, Product, and other departments to ensure that we are aligned with company policies, industry regulations and legal requirements. 

• Proactively drive quote and order execution through strategic deal structuring, ensuring they are delivered on time and within scope.

• Act as first line support for any quote creation issues for the Sales Organization. 

• Help advise and craft standards and best practices for all facets of a deal including product, operational, legal and financial. 

• Identify potential risks and issues during order creation and execution and develop mitigation plans to address them.

• Provide quote review and pricing approval support, ensuring compliance with company policy standards.

• Make recommendations for approvals for non-standard deal elements across internal stakeholders aimed at driving consistent terms and conditions.

• Work proactively to predict and minimize potential issues before they arise and resolve those in a timely manner.

• Identify opportunities to streamline and improve quote and order execution processes, driving operational efficiency and effectiveness.  

• Implement quality control measures to ensure that deliverables meet the agreed-upon standards and quality criteria.

• Communicate progress, issues, and key milestones to relevant stakeholders, including management.

YOUR EXPERIENCE

• Bachelor’s degree or global equivalent experience preferred.

• 3 - 5 years of experience in Sales Operations, Commercial support, or Finance role.

• 3 - 5 year minimum experience using Salesforce.com, CPQ, Docusign CLM (or similar order creation/execution tools).

• Proven experience in deal structuring and execution and process governance. 

• Experience with Quote and Order Form creation and special terms and conditions related to non-standard agreements. 

• Continuous improvement mindset with a focus on process optimization

title: Physical Security Lead
description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year - far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp is hiring its first dedicated Physical Security Lead to build and run the program that protects our people, our leaders, our events, and our offices. Our footprint now spans a multi-floor New York headquarters, Ramp-managed offices, and a growing set of hubs across North America and Europe. Our leaders are increasingly visible on public stages.

You'll own three areas in roughly equal measure: executive protection, event security, and office security (access control, cameras, guards, and building security). Your job is to turn a set of strong vendors and partner teams into one measurable, risk-based program.

This is a high-ownership IC role on the Corporate Security team. It reports to the Director of IT & Corporate Security and is based at our NYC HQ. This is a physical security role; cybersecurity and information security are owned by other Ramp security teams. We aren't looking for a guard supervisor or a box-checker. We want someone who makes it safe for Ramp to move fast, host great events, and keep our leaders accessible.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Build and run Ramp's executive protection program:

- Protective risk assessments and residential security reviews.

- Domestic and international travel security.

- Advance work for high-visibility appearances.

- Selecting, standing up, and managing our executive protection provider.

- Turn threat intelligence into protective action. Partner with Detection & Response to move from online threat and exposure monitoring to threat assessments, personal-information exposure reduction, and clear escalation playbooks.

- Own security for internal and external events, from all-hands and offsites to conferences, customer events, and executive dinners:

- Risk-tiered intake and written security plans.

- Coordination with venues and vendors.

- On-site leadership for the highest-risk events.

- After-action reviews.

- Set Ramp's global physical security standards for access control, video surveillance, intercoms, visitor management, and alarm monitoring. Tier them for headquarters, Ramp-managed offices, and flexible or serviced hub spaces.

- Build security into every new office, move, and expansion:

- Write the security design requirements and review drawings.

- Manage integrators through installation and acceptance testing.

- Partner with IT on network and identity integration.

- Manage the guard program and security vendors end to end: scope, post orders, SLAs and KPIs, budget, and quarterly business reviews. Own the security relationship with landlords and building management.

- Lead emergency preparedness and physical incident response:

- Emergency notifications, evacuation and shelter-in-place plans, and drills.

- Liaison with local law enforcement.

- Workplace-violence prevention, in partnership with People and Legal.

- Run physical access governance with IT. Tie access to joiner/mover/leaver events, run regular access reviews, and keep audit-ready evidence for physical security controls.

Join the Network Operations Systems Group

Do what you love

• Have a Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Computer Science, or related field

• Have at least 0.6 years experience with programming in Python, Go and/or shell script

• Have at least 0.6 years development experience on Linux/ Unix platforms

• Have knowledge of common internet protocols such as TCP/IP, HTTP, DNS and/or TLS/SSL

Cloud and Edge: Running apps closer to users for instant performance.
Security : Neutralizing threats before they ever reach your data.
Content Delivery : Scaling the world's biggest moments without a glitch.
AI : Enabling our customers to build, secure, and scale AI apps on the world's most distributed cloud platform.

At Akamai, we don't just support the internet; we power and protect it, because behind every great digital experience is a massive hidden challenge. And we're the ones who solve it. When millions of people hit play or pay, Akamai ensures it just works.
Benefits at Akamai: We support your health, well-being, finances, and life beyond work. See our benefits.
FlexBase adapts to your job's needs
Akamai's FlexBase program is yet another way we show our commitment to providing employees with an exceptional workplace experience. It's not about telling employees where to work; it's about supporting employees to do their best work.

We trust our incredible employees to work in ways that suit them best: at home, in an office, or a combination of both.

Connect with us on social and see what life at Akamai is like!

title: Community Engagement Manager, Data Centers (New York)
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history. That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate.

We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in New York to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centers are sited, built, and operated. This is not a communications role or a government affairs role, though you will do elements of both. It is a relationship role: your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbor, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations.

You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.

You will travel regularly across New York State, including upstate communities, up to 50% of the time, and occasionally to other Anthropic data center markets.

Key responsibilities

•
Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with town, village, city, and county elected officials and administrators, planning and zoning boards, local industrial development agencies, state agencies, economic development organizations, community groups, civic leaders, labor and building trades organizations, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the New York data center markets you cover

•
Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations

•
Build external coalitions, host education and listening sessions, and design local solutions that deliver real benefits to the communities where we operate

•
Represent Anthropic in public forums, town halls, planning hearings, community events, and local media

•
Monitor community sentiment and local political dynamics, and advise internal teams on risks, opportunities, and the right pace and posture for engagement

•
Partner with the Real Estate and Infrastructure team to bring community input into how projects are planned, communicated, and delivered, not just how they are announced, including public comment and environmental review processes

•
Work with the Communications team to develop proactive, locally relevant messaging

•
Coordinate charitable giving, community investment, and economic development commitments in your markets, including managing nonprofit partner relationships

•
Partner with the Energy and Sustainability team to explain our approach to environmental stewardship and respond to questions about power, water, and land use, including how New York's energy and climate policies and grid conditions shape our plans

•
Build a community engagement playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows

Minimum qualifications

•
Experience in community affairs, public affairs, economic development, government relations, local or state government, or a closely related field

title: Area Sales Manager - HVAC
description:
Category: HVAC

Location: North East United Kingdom

Our client is a well-established HVAC manufacturer, supplying air distribution solutions to commercial construction projects across the UK. With a workforce of over 250 employees, they are recognised for both product quality and technical expertise.
As part of their continued growth, the company is now seeking a Field-Based Area Sales Manager to join the external sales team and cover the North East England region.
In this role, you will:

• Develop and manage relationships across a wide range of commercial project types, including offices, healthcare, education, residential, hospitality, retail, and government buildings.

• Ensure the company’s products (e.g. diffusers, dampers, grilles, control systems) are specified, approved, and ultimately installed on new projects.

• Engage with key decision-makers throughout the route to market, including M&E consultants, main contractors, specialist subcontractors, design & build contractors, and specifiers.

This is a remote position, typically spending 3-4 days per week in the field and the remainder working from home. Project values range from £10,000 to £250,000+, with sales cycles typically spanning 6-18 months.
In addition to managing regional enquiries and driving business development, you’ll also represent the company at conferences and exhibitions alongside the National Sales Manager and Sales Director.

Requirements
We are keen to hear from:

• Candidates from a wholesale or distribution background who are looking to move into technical sales.

• Experienced specification-led sales engineers with knowledge of HVAC or related products and an understanding of the route to market, ideally gained with another manufacturer.

• Field sales experience with a wholesaler, distributor, or manufacturer within the construction industry.

• HVAC product knowledge is highly desirable, but we will also consider candidates from other technical field-based products or services such as lighting, facades, renewables, lifts & escalators, fire & security systems.

• Strong understanding of the route to market, including engagement with M&E consultants, main contractors, subcontractors, or specifiers throughout the project lifecycle.

• Comfortable working autonomously, managing your own diary and territory.

• A full UK driving licence is essential.

Benefits

• £45,000-£55,000 base salary negotiable

• OTE first year £15,000

• Company car, phone and laptop

• Good company pension

• Life insurance

title: Sales Specialist - Patient Support Coordinator (Remote, Telehealth)
description:
This is a remote position.
Location: Remote (Philippines) · Schedule: Full-time, US Pacific Time (PST) · Compensation : $7-$8 USD per hour (contractor)
About Shapely

Shapely is transforming weight loss care through a physician-led, evidence-based model that makes treatment affordable and accessible. We pair clinical excellence with a seamless integrated app to help patients achieve sustainable, long-lasting results. As we scale across multiple states, we're hiring a Sales Specialist - Patient Support Coordinator to be the first point of contact for prospective patients and guide them into care.
As our Sales Specialist, you'll be the first voice many prospective patients hear. You'll connect with warm leads who have already expressed interest, help them understand our program, answer their questions about eligibility and cost, and convert that interest into a scheduled appointment. It's a consultative, phone-based sales role in a healthcare setting - equal parts persuasion and genuine care.
This is a full-time, remote contractor role on a Pacific Time (PST) schedule, with room to grow and a supportive team behind you.
What You'll Do
1. Outbound Lead Engagement - the core of the role

• Make outbound sales calls and follow-ups to prospective patients who have expressed interest in Shapely .

• Educate leads on our program, our physician-led model, and how GLP-1/GIP weight loss medications work.

• Explain insurance eligibility basics and general coverage considerations to set accurate expectations.

• Guide interested leads through enrollment and schedule their initial appointment.

2. Pipeline & Conversion Management

• Manage your pipeline of leads in the CRM, tracking follow-ups and conversion status.

• Meet or exceed targets for outbound calls, conversions, and scheduled appointments.

• Re-engage warm leads who haven't yet enrolled to answer outstanding questions and move them forward.

3. Cross-Team Coordination

• Partner with our Prior Authorization and Concierge teams to ensure a smooth handoff once a patient enrolls.

• Relay common objections, questions, and friction points to leadership to help refine our messaging and process.

Requirements

Must-Have

•

Summary

We are seeking a talented individual for a Lead Associate, Itemized Bill Review Quality Auditor to perform reviews of medical records, healthcare claims, itemized medical bill, and UB-04 forms to ensure accuracy, compliance, and proper billing practices. This role is responsible for conducting quality assurance audits and oversight of itemized bill review activities to ensure accuracy, consistency, regulatory compliance, and alignment with client-specific review methodologies. This role serves as a subject matter expert in hospital billing, reimbursement methodologies, payment integrity, and claim auditing.

The Lead Associate performs comprehensive quality reviews of itemized bill audits completed by clinical and coding review staff, validates audit findings, and provides regulatory and reimbursement support for determination decisions. This position requires extensive knowledge of hospital charging practices, revenue codes, UB-04 billing requirements, CMS reimbursement methodologies, NCCI edits, and payment integrity concepts. The individual is expected to identify opportunities for quality improvement, provide staff education and mentoring, and support the achievement of departmental quality and performance goals.

Your role in our mission

• Perform quality audits of itemized bill reviews to ensure accuracy, consistency, compliance, and proper documentation.

• Validate audit findings by reviewing itemized bills, medical records, claims, contracts, fee schedules, and supporting documentation.

• Evaluate billing errors, duplicate charges, unsupported services, coding, modifiers, units, reimbursement methods, and compliance requirements.

• Conduct complex audits of institutional claims, itemized bills, and medical records to identify inaccuracies, payment issues, and compliance concerns.

• Review inpatient, outpatient, emergency, ambulatory surgery, and ancillary service charges for billing and reimbursement accuracy.

• Assess revenue codes, charge capture practices, HCPCS, CPT, ICD-10 support, and payer requirements.

• Identify payment integrity opportunities through billing and reimbursement reviews.

• Serve as a subject matter expert in business proposals and assist with training, mentoring, and educating new reviewers.

• Maintain current clinical and coding knowledge and cross-train across multiple claim types to support client needs.

What we're looking for

• Associate degree in Health Information Management, Nursing, Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, or related healthcare field required.

• Certified Coder or Registered Nurse with Coding Experience. One of the following Coding Certifications preferred: RHIA, RHIT, CCS, CIC, CPMA, CCDS, COC or CPC

• Comprehensive knowledge of Revenue Codes, CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10 Coding Guidelines, Charge Master structure, UB-O4 billing requirements, APC, ASC, OPPS, DRG reimbursement methodology.

• Advanced knowledge of hospital billing practices, itemized bill review methodologies, and payment integrity concepts.

• Contribuer à l’évaluation des programmes, à l’expansion des services, à la mise en œuvre de nouvelles initiatives ainsi qu’aux projets de recherche ou pilotes, d’un point de vue clinique.

• Expérience en soins virtuels, en télésanté ou en services de santé numériques fortement souhaitée.

• Expérience démontrée en assurance qualité, gouvernance médicale, recherche ou évaluation de projets pilotes.

• Expérience dans l’interprétation de lignes directrices cliniques, l’élaboration de protocoles ou l’examen de pratiques fondées sur des données probantes.

• Expérience de collaboration avec des partenaires du système de santé, des organismes gouvernementaux ou des associations professionnelles (un atout).

• Connaissance démontrée du système de santé du Nouveau-Brunswick, y compris les soins primaires, les autorités sanitaires régionales et les programmes de santé provinciaux.

Qualifications / Formation

• Diplôme en médecine (MD ou équivalent) d’une faculté de médecine reconnue.

• Médecin autorisé et en règle auprès du Collège des médecins et chirurgiens du Nouveau-Brunswick (CMCNB).

• Autorisé à exercer et à détenir des privilèges au sein du Réseau de santé Horizon et du Réseau de santé Vitalité.

• Expérience clinique récente en soins primaires, soins urgents, médecine d’urgence ou autres spécialités pertinentes.

Qualifications / Compétences et aptitudes :

• Excellente connaissance des normes réglementaires et professionnelles applicables aux médecins du Nouveau-Brunswick.

• Capacité d’analyser des données cliniques, d’identifier des tendances et de formuler des recommandations non contraignantes.

• Expérience ou aisance avec les systèmes de DME/DSE, les applications de soins virtuels et les outils CRM à des fins de supervision de programme, de conseils et de suivi
